clue.text: Mistakenly, one's open to receive the other disease

definitions.text: Mistakenly, one's open to receive the other disease

parts.words: Mistakenly, one's open to receive the other disease
parts.note: putting your foot in your mouth is a blunder: the mouth, open, mistakenly takes in the foot; the whole phrase also names a livestock illness

explanation.surface: A puzzling account of an illness in which one body part accidentally swallows another.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'put your foot in it' or in your mouth is to say something tactless, so the mouth is 'open to receive the other' by mistake; the two body parts together name the cattle illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly infectious viral illness of cloven-hoofed livestock carries this two-body-part name.

clue.text: Drake is undermining foreign power no end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drake' looks like a duck or the sailor's surname; it is the surname whose first name is wanted. 'no end' cuts FRANCE to FRANC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan navigator, so his first name is clued by his surname.
